paragraphs: Unless the context requires otherwise, the terms "Owens Corning," "Company," "we," "its," and "our" in this Annual Report on Form 10-K refer to Owens Corning and its subsidiaries.

Owens Corning is a building products leader committed to building a sustainable future through material innovation. Our products provide durable, sustainable, and energy-efficient solutions that leverage our unique capabilities and market-leading positions to help our customers win and grow. Our roofing products and systems enhance curb appeal and protect people's homes. Our insulation products conserve energy and improve acoustics, fire resistance and air quality in the spaces where people live, work and play. Our doors and door systems provide comfort, safety and style for the interior and exterior of homes.

We are global in scope, human in scale with approximately 25,000 total employees in 31 countries dedicated to generating value for our customers and shareholders and making a difference in the communities where we work and live. Founded in 1938 and based in Toledo, Ohio, Owens Corning recorded net sales in 2025 of $10.1 billion.

On February 13, 2025, the Company entered into a definitive agreement ("GR Agreement") for the sale of our global glass reinforcements ("GR") business for a purchase price of approximately $436 million, less costs to sell. As of December 31, 2025, the estimated purchase price was $474 million, net of cash, less costs to sell. The change since signing is due to the changes in customary and transaction-specific price adjustments which are subject to further changes through the date of the final closing adjustments. The GR business, historically part of the Company's Composites segment, manufactures, fabricates, and sells glass fiber reinforcements for a wide variety of applications in wind energy, infrastructure, industrial, transportation and consumer markets. The sale will complete Owens Corning's review of strategic alternatives for the business, as previously announced on February 9, 2024, and aligns with the strategy to reshape the Company to focus on building products in North America and Europe. The transaction is expected to close in the first few months of 2026 and is subject to customary regulatory approvals and other conditions.

The transaction represents a strategic shift that has a major effect on the Company's operations and financial results. Effective January 1, 2025, the GR business's financial results are reflected in the Company's consolidated financial statements as discontinued operations for all periods presented.

Effective January 1, 2025, due to a strategic shift in how we manage our business as a result of the GR Agreement and the classification of the GR business as a discontinued operation, we changed the composition of our reportable segments. As a result, all prior period information was recast to reflect this change. The Company now has three reportable segments: Roofing, Insulation and Doors.

On May 15, 2024, the Company acquired all of the outstanding shares of Masonite International Corporation ("Masonite"), a leading global designer, manufacturer, marketer and distributor of interior and exterior doors and door systems for the residential new construction and residential repair and remodeling markets. The addition of Masonite's market-leading doors business, reported as the Doors segment, creates a new growth platform for the Company, strengthening the Company's position in building and construction and expanding its offering of branded residential building products.

At December 31, 2025, the Company had an integrated business model with three reportable segments: Roofing, Insulation, and Doors, which accounted for approximately 43%, 36% and 21% of our total reportable segment net sales, respectively, in 2025.

Our primary products in the Roofing segment are laminate asphalt roofing shingles. Other products include roofing components, composite lumber and oxidized asphalt primarily used in residential construction. Roofing also manufactures and sells glass mat and specialty veil materials used in building and construction applications We have been able to service the growing demand for longer lasting, aesthetically attractive laminate products with efficient capital investment.

We sell shingles and roofing components primarily through distributors, home centers and lumberyards in the United States. Oxidized asphalt is a significant input used in the production of our asphalt roofing shingles. We are vertically integrated and have manufacturing facilities that process asphalt for use in our roofing shingles manufacturing process. In addition, we sell processed asphalt to other shingle manufacturers, to roofing contractors for built-up roofing asphalt systems and to manufacturers in a variety of other industries, including automotive, chemical, rubber and construction. Asphalt input costs and third-party asphalt sales prices are correlated to crude oil prices.

Glass nonwoven mat is a significant input used in the production of our asphalt shingles. The mat uses wet use chopped strand produced by our Insulation segment. We also sell glass nonwoven mat and specialty veil materials to downstream manufacturers for the production of various applications, including vinyl flooring, gypsum wall boards, ceiling tiles and battery separators. These customers span across many industries including building and construction, industrial and infrastructure and renewable energy.

Demand for products in our Roofing segment is generally driven by both residential repair and remodeling activity and by new residential construction. Roofing damage from major storms can significantly increase demand in this segment. As a result, sales in this segment do not always follow seasonal home improvement, remodeling and new construction industry patterns.

Our Roofing segment competes primarily with asphalt shingle manufacturers in the United States. According to various industry reports and Company estimates, Owens Corning's Roofing segment is the second largest producer of asphalt roofing shingles in the United States. Principal methods of competition include innovation and product design, breadth of product offering, proximity to customers, quality and price.

Our manufacturing operations are generally continuous in nature, and we warehouse much of our production prior to sale since we operate with relatively short delivery cycles. One of the raw materials important to this segment is sourced from a sole supplier. We have a long-term supply contract for this material and have no reason to believe that any availability issues will exist. If this supply was to become unavailable, our production could be interrupted until such time as the supplies again became available or the Company reformulated its products. Additionally, the supply of asphalt, another significant raw material in this segment, has been constricted at times. Although this has not caused a significant interruption of our production in the past, prolonged asphalt shortages would restrict our ability to produce products in this segment.

Our efforts in acquiring and integrating other businesses, establishing joint ventures, expanding our production capacity or divesting assets are subject to a number of risks.

Emerging issues related to our development, integration and use of artificial intelligence ("AI") could give rise to legal or regulatory action, damage our reputation or otherwise materially harm our business.

We could face potential product liability and warranty claims, we may not accurately estimate costs related to such claims, and we may not have sufficient insurance coverage available to cover such claims.

paragraphs: We discuss in this section some of the risk factors that could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, value and results of operations. You should consider these risk factors in connection with evaluating the forward-looking statements contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K because these risk factors could cause our actual results and financial condition to differ materially from those projected in forward-looking statements.

The Company maintains processes that aim to manage enterprise risks through identification and mitigation of those risks. Despite our efforts, we may fail to identify or mitigate certain risks, which could have a material and adverse impact on our business, financial condition, value and results of operations in future periods.
MACROECONOMIC, MARKET AND OPERATIONAL RISKS

A large portion of our products are used in the markets for residential and non-residential construction and repair and remodeling. Demand for certain of our products is affected in part by the level of new residential construction in the United States and elsewhere, although typically not until a number of months after the change in the level of construction. Lower demand in the regions and markets where our products are sold results in lower revenues and lower profitability. Historically, construction activity has been cyclical and is influenced by prevailing economic conditions, including the level of interest rates and availability of financing, inflation, employment levels, consumer spending habits, consumer confidence and other macroeconomic factors outside our control. Interest rates increased substantially in the past few years, remained high with slight decreases in 2025, and are currently expected to decrease further but stay relatively high in 2026. The combination of high interest rates and high levels of inflation reduces the affordability of mortgages and other financing options, and increases the cost of home improvement projects. These trends have likely resulted in reduced levels of repair and remodel as well as new construction activity and demand for our products. Additionally, market reactions to the U.S. government's policies and stances have created economic uncertainty, leading to fluctuations in inflation and interest rates. Due to this uncertainty, we cannot predict if or when interest rates or inflation levels will stabilize or the impact that this uncertainty may have on repair and remodel activity, new construction activity, demand for our products, our business generally, or our financial condition.

Residential and non-residential construction is also affected by the cost and availability of skilled labor, which could impact both the cost and pace of construction activity, as well as the construction methods used, all of which could adversely affect demand for our products.

In addition, a portion of our annual product demand is attributable to the repair of damage caused by severe storms. The frequency and magnitude of severe storms can have a significant impact on the markets for residential and non-residential construction, repair and improvement projects. In periods with below average levels of severe storms, demand for such products is reduced.

paragraphs: This Management's Discussion and Analysis ("MD&A") is intended to help investors understand Owens Corning, our operations and our present business environment. MD&A is provided as a supplement to, and should be read in conjunction with, our Consolidated Financial Statements and the accompanying Notes thereto contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Unless the context requires otherwise, the terms "Owens Corning," "Company," "we," "its," and "our" in this Annual Report on Form 10-K refer to Owens Corning and its subsidiaries.

This section of this Annual Report on Form 10-K generally discusses 2025 and 2024 items and year-to-year comparisons between 2025 and 2024. Discussions of 2023 items and year-to-year comparisons between 2024 and 2023 that are not included in this Form 10-K can be found in "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" in Part II, Item 7 of the Company's Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024.

Owens Corning is a building products leader committed to building a sustainable future through material innovation. As described below, the Company has three reportable segments: Roofing, Insulation and Doors. Through these lines of business, the Company manufactures and sells products that provide durable, sustainable and energy-efficient solutions. We are a market leader in many of our major product categories.

Net (loss) earnings from continuing operations attributable to Owens Corning were a loss of $188 million in 2025, compared to earnings of $947 million in 2024. The Company generated $2,268 million in adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization ("Adjusted EBITDA") from continuing operations in 2025, compared to $2,468 million in 2024. See the Adjusted Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization From Continuing Operations section of the MD&A for further information regarding Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations, including the reconciliation to Net (loss) earnings from continuing operations attributable to Owens Corning. Segment earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization ("EBITDA") performance compared to 2024 decreased $121 million in our Roofing segment, decreased $97 million in our Insulation segment and remained flat in our Doors segment. Within our Corporate, Other and Eliminations category, General corporate expenses and other decreased by $18 million.

In 2025, as a result of interim goodwill impairment testing, we recorded $1,135 million in pre-tax non-cash impairment charges, equal to the excess of the Doors reporting unit's carrying value over its fair value. The remaining balance of goodwill for the Doors reporting unit of $380 million as of December 31, 2025 continues to be at risk for future impairment.

On May 13, 2025, the Board of Directors approved the 2025 Repurchase Authorization. The 2025 Repurchase Authorization enables the Company to repurchase shares through the open market, privately negotiated, or other transactions. The actual number of shares repurchased will depend on timing, market conditions and other factors and will be at the Company's discretion. This authorization is in addition to the previously announced share repurchase program.

On February 13, 2025, the Company entered into the GR agreement for the sale of our global GR business for a purchase price of approximately $436 million, less costs to sell. As of December 31, 2025, the estimated purchase price was $474 million, net of cash, and less costs to sell. The change since signing is due to the changes in customary and transaction-specific price adjustments which are subject to further changes through the date of the final closing adjustments. The GR business, historically part of the Company's Composites segment, manufactures, fabricates, and sells glass fiber reinforcements for a wide variety of applications in wind energy, infrastructure, industrial, transportation and consumer markets. The sale will complete Owens Corning's review of strategic alternatives for the business, announced on February 9, 2024, and aligns with the strategy to reshape the Company to focus on residential and commercial building products in North America and Europe. The transaction is expected to close in the first few months of 2026 and is subject to customary regulatory approvals and other conditions.
ITEM 7. MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS (continued)

The transaction represents a strategic shift that has a major effect on the Company's operations and financial results. Effective January 1, 2025, the GR business' financial results are reflected in the Company's consolidated financial statements as discontinued operations for all periods presented. During the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, net loss from discontinued operations attributable to Owens Corning was $334 million on the Consolidated Statement of Earnings, primarily related to the loss recognized upon the classification of the GR business into discontinued operations. The loss on discontinued operations was determined by comparing the carrying value of the discontinued operation to the fair value of the business, as derived from the signed GR Agreement, less estimated costs to sell.

As a result of classifying the GR business as a discontinued operation, a portion of the Goodwill from our former Composites reporting unit was allocated to the Balance Sheets of the discontinued operation as of March 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024. As of the date of classification of the GR business as a discontinued operation, the Company determined the amount of Goodwill to allocate based on the relative fair values of the discontinued operation and the former Composites reporting unit. This resulted in an allocation of $98 million of Goodwill to the discontinued operation.

After allocating Goodwill to the discontinued operation, the Company compared the carrying value of the discontinued operation to the fair value of the discontinued operation, defined as the sale price less estimated selling costs. During the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, the Company incurred a pre-tax loss on classification as discontinued operations of $451 million.

Effective January 1, 2025, due to a strategic shift in how we manage our business as a result of the GR Agreement and the classification of the GR business as a discontinued operation, we changed the composition of our reportable segments. As a result, all prior period information was recast to reflect this change. The Company now has three reportable segments: Roofing, Insulation and Doors.

Beginning in the first quarter of 2025, the U.S. government announced additional tariffs on goods imported into the U.S. from numerous countries and multiple nations have responded with reciprocal tariffs and other actions. The Company continues to monitor the economic effects of such announcements. The Company has implemented short- and long-term mitigation efforts. Based on the current tariff policies, the Company expects to partially offset the operating profit impact of the enacted tariffs with supply chain adjustments and productivity and cost savings actions. To the extent additional tariffs or other trade restrictions are enacted and the Company is unable to offset the tariffs or the tariffs negatively impact demand, the Company's revenue and profitability could be adversely impacted.
ITEM 7. MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS (continued)

paragraphs: 除非文意另有要求，本年度10-K申報書中之"Owens Corning","Company","we","its"及"our"皆指Owens Corning及其子公司。
Owens Corning為一領導的建築產品供應商，致力於透過材料創新來建立可持續的未來。我們的產品提供耐用、可持續且節能的解決方案，利用我們獨特的技術與市場領導地位，協助客戶獲利與成長。我們的屋頂產品與系統可提升建築外觀並保護人們的家。我們的絕熱產品可節省能源並改善人們居住、工作與娛樂空間的音響效果、防火性能與空氣品質。我們的門與門系統則提供居家內外的舒適、安全與風格。
我們在全球範圍內運作，規模則以人數為主，約有25,000名總員工分佈於31個國家，致力於為客戶與股東創造價值，並在所工作與居住的社區中產生正面影響。Owens Corning於1938年成立，總部設於美國俄亥俄州託萊多市，2025年的淨銷售額為101億美元。

2025年2月13日，本公司與買方簽訂了買賣協議（"GR Agreement"），出售我們的全球玻璃增強材料（"GR"）業務，買價約為436億美元，扣除賣方成本。截至2025年12月31日，預估買價為474億美元，扣除現金及賣方成本。自簽約以來的變動係因常規及交易特定的價格調整變動所致，此等調整可能在最終結算日進一步變動。GR業務，歷史為本公司Composites分部之一，製造、加工並銷售玻璃纖維增強材料，應用於風能、基礎建設、工業、運輸及消費市場。此交易完成本公司對該業務戰略選擇的評估，如2024年2月9日所公告，並符合本公司重新定位以專注於北美與歐洲建築產品的戰略。交易預計於2026年初完成，並需經常規監管機構批准及其他條件。
此交易代表一項戰略轉變，對本公司運作與財務結果產生重大影響。自2025年1月1日起，GR業務的財務結果已於本公司合併財務報表中列為已終止營運業務，適用於所有期間。
自2025年1月1日起，因應本公司因GR Agreement而對業務管理方式的戰略轉變，並將GR業務歸類為已終止營運業務，本公司已調整應報告分部的組成。因此，所有過往期間資訊已重新整理以反映此變動。本公司現有三個應報告分部：屋頂、絕熱與門。

2024年5月15日，本公司取得Masonite International Corporation（"Masonite"）所有發行在外的股權，Masonite為全球領先的內外門與門系統設計、製造、行銷與分銷公司，專門服務住宅新建與住宅修繕與改建市場。Masonite市場領導地位的門業務，被歸類為門分部，為本公司創造新的成長平台，強化本公司在建築與建設領域的競爭地位，並擴展其品牌住宅建築產品的提供。
截至2025年12月31日，本公司擁有整合的業務模式，包含三個應報告分部：屋頂、絕熱與門，分別佔2025年總應報告分部淨銷售額約43%、36%與21%。
本公司應報告分部 Roofing 的主要產品為複合式瀝青瓦片。其他產品包括瓦片零組件、複合木材及氧化瀝青，主要用於住宅建設。Roofing 還製造並銷售用於建築與建設應用的玻璃纖維網與特殊覆蓋材料。本公司已能透過高效的資本投資，應對對更長壽命且外觀吸引人的複合產品日益增長的需求。
本公司主要透過經銷商、家居中心及木材倉庫在美國銷售瓦片與瓦片零組件。氧化瀝青是製造本公司瀝青瓦片的主要原料之一。本公司為垂直整合型企業，擁有製造廠房處理瀝青以供瓦片製造使用。此外，本公司亦將處理過的瀝青銷售給其他瓦片製造商、 roofing 承包商用於建築用瀝青系統，以及多種其他產業的製造商，包括汽車、化學、橡膠與建設業。瀝青原料成本與第三方瀝青銷售價格與原油價格相關聯。
玻璃非織造纖維網是本公司製造瀝青瓦片的重要原料。該纖維網使用本公司 Insulation 分部製造的濕用切斷纖維。本公司亦將玻璃非織造纖維網與特殊覆蓋材料銷售給下游製造商，用於製造各種應用，包括乙烯基地板、石膏板、天花板磚與電池隔板。這些客戶來自多個產業，包括建築與建設、工業與基礎設施以及可再生能源。
本公司 Roofing 分部產品的需求通常由住宅修繕與翻修活動以及新住宅建設所驅動。重大風暴造成的 roofing 損壞可能顯著提高此分部的需求。因此，此分部的銷售並不一定遵循住宅改善、翻修與新建設施業的季節性模式。
本公司 Roofing 分部主要與美國的瀝青瓦片製造商競爭。根據各項產業報告與本公司估計，Owens Corning 的 Roofing 分部為美國第二大瀝青瓦片製造商。主要競爭方式包括創新與產品設計、產品種類的廣度、距離客戶的距離、品質與價格。

本公司製造作業通常為連續性作業，且本公司在銷售前會將大部分生產產品存放於倉庫，因為本公司運作的交貨週期相對較短。此分部重要的原料之一來自單一供應商。本公司與該原料供應商有長期供應契約，且本公司無理由相信會有供應問題。若此原料無法取得，本公司生產可能中斷，直至原料重新取得或本公司重新調整產品配方為止。此外，瀝青為此分部另一重要原料，有時會出現供應緊縮。儘管過去未造成本公司生產的重大中斷，但長期瀝青短缺將限制本公司在此分部的生產能力。

paragraphs: 本公司的管理層討論與分析（"MD&A"）旨在協助投資人瞭解 Owens Corning、我們的業務運作及目前的營運環境。MD&A 是作為補充，並應與本年度 10-K 報告所附的合併財務報表及其附註一併閱讀。除非文意另有要求，否則本 10-K 報告中 "Owens Corning"、"Company"、"we"、"its" 及 "our" 一詞均指 Owens Corning 及其子公司。
本年度 10-K 報告此部分一般討論 2025 年及 2024 年的項目，以及 2025 年與 2024 年之間的年對年比較。未包含於本 10-K 報告中的 2023 年項目及 2024 年與 2023 年之間的年對年比較，可參閱 "財務狀況與營運成果之管理層討論與分析"，位於公司 2024 年 12 月 31 日財務年度 10-K 報告之第二部分，第 7 項。
Owens Corning 是一家建築產品領導者，致力於透過材料創新打造可持續的未來。如下列所述，本公司有三個應報告分部：屋頂、絕熱材料與門窗。透過這些業務線，本公司製造並銷售提供耐用、可持續及節能解決方案的產品。我們在許多主要產品類別中都是市場領導者。

2025 年，來自持續運營業務的淨虧損歸屬於 Owens Corning 為 1.88 億美元，與 2024 年的盈利 9.47 億美元相比。2025 年，本公司來自持續運營業務的調整後營業息稅折舊及 amortization（"Adjusted EBITDA"）為 226.8 億美元，與 2024 年的 246.8 億美元相比。請參閱 MD&A 中的 "調整後營業息稅折舊及 amortization 從持續運營業務" 部分，以取得更多關於調整後持續運營業務 EBITDA 的資訊，包括與淨虧損歸屬於 Owens Corning 從持續運營業務的調整後 EBITDA 的對應關係。各分部的息稅折舊及 amortization（"EBITDA"）表現與 2024 年相比，屋頂分部減少 1.21 億美元，絕熱材料分部減少 9,700 萬美元，門窗分部維持不變。在本公司、其他及消除項目類別中，一般企業費用及其他項目減少 1,800 萬美元。
2025 年，由於中期商譽減損測試，我們記錄了 113.5 億美元的預提非現金減損費用，等於門窗報告單位帳面價值超過公允價值的差額。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，門窗報告單位的商譽餘額為 38 億美元，仍可能因未來減損而受到風險影響。
2025 年 5 月 13 日，董事會批准了 2025 年股份回購授權。2025 年股份回購授權使本公司可以透過公開市場、私下協議或其他交易方式回購股份。實際回購的股份數量將取決於時間、市場條件及其他因素，並由本公司自行決定。此授權為此前宣佈的股份回購計劃之補充。

2025 年 2 月 13 日，本公司與 GR 約定，出售我們的全球 GR 事業，買價約為 43.6 億美元，扣除出售成本。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，預估買價為 47.4 億美元，扣除現金及出售成本。自簽約以來的變動是因為常規及交易特定的價格調整變動，這些調整可能在最終關閉調整日之前進一步變動。GR 事業，歷來屬於本公司 Composites 分部，製造、加工並銷售用於風能、基礎建設、工業、運輸及消費市場的玻璃纖維增強材料。此交易將完成本公司於 2024 年 2 月 9 日宣佈的業務戰略替代方案評估，並符合本公司重組策略，專注於北美及歐洲的住宅及商業建築產品。此交易預計於 2026 年前幾個月完成，並需經常規監管批准及其他條件。
第 7 項 管理層討論與分析財務狀況與營運成果（續）

此交易代表一項戰略轉變，對本公司的營運及財務結果有重大影響。自2025年1月1日起，GR業務的財務結果已反映於本公司的合併財務報表中，作為已終止營運業務，適用所有期間。在2025年12月31日止十二個月期間，歸屬於Owens Corning的已終止營運業務淨虧損為3.34億美元，於合併損益表中，主要係因將GR業務歸類為已終止營運業務而認列的虧損。已終止營運業務的虧損係透過比較已終止營運業務的帳面價值與根據簽訂的GR協議所衍生的業務公平價值，扣除預估出售成本後計算得出。
由於將GR業務歸類為已終止營運業務，我們前一時期Composites報告分部的商譽中，一部分已重新歸屬至已終止營運業務的資產負債表中，於2025年3月31日及2024年12月35日。於將GR業務歸類為已終止營運業務的日期，本公司根據已終止營運業務與前一時期Composites報告分部的相對公平價值，決定應歸屬的商譽金額。此舉導致歸屬至已終止營運業務的商譽為9.8億美元。
在將商譽歸屬至已終止營運業務後，本公司比較已終止營運業務的帳面價值與已終止營運業務的公平價值，定義為出售價格扣除預估出售成本。在2025年12月31日止十二個月期間，本公司因歸類為已終止營運業務而產生的預稅虧損為4.51億美元。
自2025年1月1日起，由於因GR協議及將GR業務歸類為已終止營運業務而導致本公司營運管理方式的戰略轉變，本公司已改變應報告分部的組成。因此，所有先前期間的資訊已重新整理以反映此變動。本公司現有三個應報告分部：屋頂、絕熱材料與門。

自2025年第一季起，美國政府宣佈對從多個國家進口至美國的商品加徵額外關稅，多個國家也以反制關稅及其他措施回應。本公司持續監測這些公告的經濟影響。本公司已實施短期與長期的緩衝措施。根據目前的關稅政策，本公司預期透過供應鏈調整與生產力及成本節省措施，部分抵消已實施關稅對營運利潤的影響。若未來有額外關稅或其他貿易限制措施實施，且本公司無法抵消關稅或關稅對需求產生負面影響，本公司營收與獲利可能受到不利影響。

本公司維持一些流程，旨在透過識別與緩解風險來管理企業風險。儘管我們已盡力而為，我們仍可能未能識別或緩解某些風險，這可能會對我們未來期間的業務、財務狀況、價值及營運結果產生重大且不利的影響。
總體經濟、市場與營運風險

我們產品的大部分用於住宅與非住宅建設與修繕及翻修市場。某些我們產品的需求部分受到美國及其他地區新住宅建設活動水平的影響，雖然通常在建設活動水平變動數個月後才會反映出來。我們產品銷售地區與市場的低需求會導致較低的收入與較低的獲利能力。歷來，建設活動具有週期性，並受當前經濟條件影響，包括利率水平與融資可得性、通貨膨脹、就業水平、消費者支出習慣、消費者信心及其他我們無法控制的總體經濟因素。過去幾年利率大幅上升，2025年維持高檔並略有下降，目前預期2026年利率會進一步下降但仍維持相對高檔。高利率與高通貨膨脹的組合會降低房貸及其他融資選項的負擔能力，並提高住宅改善專案的成本。這些趨勢可能導致修繕與翻修活動及新住宅建設活動減少，進而降低我們產品的需求。此外，市場對美國政府政策與立場的反應已造成經濟不確定性，導致通貨膨脹與利率波動。由於這種不確定性，我們無法預測利率或通貨膨脹水平是否會穩定，以及這種不確定性可能對修繕與翻修活動、新住宅建設活動、我們產品的需求、我們業務整體或財務狀況產生的影響。
住宅與非住宅建設也受到技術工人成本與可得性的影響，這可能會影響建設活動的成本與速度，以及所使用的建設方法，所有這些都可能對我們產品的需求產生不利影響。
此外，我們年度產品需求的一部分來自於嚴重氣候災害所造成的損壞修復。嚴重氣候災害的頻率與規模會對住宅與非住宅建設、修繕及改善專案的市場產生重大影響。在嚴重氣候災害低於平均水平的時期，這些產品的需求會減少。
